title: Exterior waves, absorbing boundaries and PML

items.title: Cartesian complex-stretch PML for a homogeneous Helmholtz mode
items.statement:
Let $k>0$, $x\in\mathbb R$ be the Cartesian normal coordinate, and $y\in\mathbb R^2$ the tangential coordinate. Let $\sigma$ be nonnegative, continuous, piecewise $C^1$, and zero for $x\le0$. Define
$$S(x)=\int_0^x\sigma(t)\,dt,\qquad X(x)=x+iS(x),\qquad s(x)=X'(x)=1+i\sigma(x).$$
The pulled-back constant-coefficient Helmholtz operator in the layer is
$$\frac1{s(x)}\partial_x\left(\frac1{s(x)}\partial_x\right)+\Delta_y+k^2.$$
This definition concerns the homogeneous Cartesian branch only; it makes no claim for heterogeneous media, curved stretches, grazing or evanescent uniform attenuation, discretizations, or finite-element convergence.

references.title: Steven G. Johnson, Notes on Perfectly Matched Layers (PMLs), §§3.1–3.2
Michler, Demkowicz, Kurtz, and Pardo, Improving the performance of Perfectly Matched Layers by means of hp-adaptivity, §§2.1–2.2

items.title: First-order local impedance condition at an artificial plane
items.statement: Use the outgoing time convention $e^{-i\omega t}$. On an artificial boundary with outward unit normal $n$, the first-order local impedance condition is $\partial_nu-iku=0$. For the plane $x=R$ with $n=+e_x$, this is $\partial_xu-iku=0$. It is the exact outgoing relation at normal incidence and an approximation for oblique propagating modes; no exactness or uniform small-reflection claim at grazing incidence is part of this definition.

references.title: Galkowski, Lafontaine, and Spence, Local absorbing boundary conditions on fixed domains give order-one errors for high-frequency waves
NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, Chapter 10: Bessel Functions

items.title: Perfect matching and attenuation for non-grazing propagating modes
items.statement:
Let $k>0$, $\eta\in\mathbb R^2$ satisfy $|\eta|<k$, and let $q=\sqrt{k^2-|\eta|^2}>0$ be the outgoing normal branch. In the stretch of [[def-pe18-cartesian-complex-stretch-pml]],
$$u(x,y)=e^{iqX(x)+i\eta\cdot y}$$
solves the pulled-back Helmholtz equation. At $x=0$, its value and normal flux $(1/s)\partial_xu$ agree with those of the physical mode $e^{iqx+i\eta\cdot y}$. Its modulus is $e^{-qS(x)}$. If a family of modes satisfies $q\ge q_0>0$, then $|u(x,y)|\le e^{-q_0S(x)}$ uniformly; whenever $S(x)\ge\sigma_0x$ for some $\sigma_0>0$, this is at most $e^{-q_0\sigma_0x}$. No uniform bound is asserted as $q\downarrow0$.

references.title: Steven G. Johnson, Notes on Perfectly Matched Layers (PMLs), §§3.1–3.2
Michler, Demkowicz, Kurtz, and Pardo, Improving the performance of Perfectly Matched Layers by means of hp-adaptivity, §§2.1–2.2

items.title: Spherical Hankel modulus and uniform radial bounds
items.statement:
For integers $\ell\ge0$ and real $z>0$, write $h_\ell=h_\ell^{(1)}$ using [[def-spherical-bessel-and-hankel-functions]]. Then
$$|h_\ell(z)|^2=\sum_{m=0}^{\ell}S_{\ell m}z^{-2m-2},\qquad S_{\ell m}=\frac{(2m)!(\ell+m)!}{4^m(m!)^2(\ell-m)!}.$$
Consequently $|h_\ell(z)|$ is nonincreasing in $z$, $|h_{\ell-1}(z)|\le|h_\ell(z)|$ for $\ell\ge1$, and $|h_\ell'(z)|\le(1+(\ell+1)/z)|h_\ell(z)|$. For every fixed $z_0>0$ and all $z\ge z_0$,
$$\frac{|z(h_\ell'(z)-ih_\ell(z))|}{|h_\ell(z_0)|}\le(\ell+1)e^{2z_0}.$$

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §§10.49–10.52
Plamen Stefanov, Scattering and Inverse Scattering in R^n, graduate lecture notes

items.title: Exact plane-wave reflection coefficient of the local impedance condition
items.statement:
For $0<q\le k$ and tangential wavevector $\eta\in\mathbb R^2$ satisfying $q^2+|\eta|^2=k^2$, consider
$$u(x,y)=e^{i\eta\cdot y}\left(e^{iq(x-R)}+\mathcal R e^{-iq(x-R)}\right).$$
The impedance condition [[def-pe18-local-impedance-absorbing-boundary]] gives
$$\mathcal R=\frac{q-k}{q+k},\qquad |\mathcal R|=\frac{k-q}{k+q}.$$
Thus reflection is zero at normal incidence $q=k$ and its magnitude tends to one as $q\downarrow0$ (grazing incidence).

references.title: Galkowski, Lafontaine, and Spence, Local absorbing boundary conditions on fixed domains give order-one errors for high-frequency waves
Steven G. Johnson, Notes on Perfectly Matched Layers (PMLs), §2

items.title: Exact reflected-mode error from a finite Dirichlet-terminated PML
items.statement:
For $q>0$, $A\ne0$, and a finite layer $0\le x\le L$ with $S(L)>0$, let a one-dimensional mode be $u(x)=Ae^{iqX(x)}+Be^{-iqX(x)}$, with the PML stretch from [[def-pe18-cartesian-complex-stretch-pml]]. Imposing $u(L)=0$ gives the reflected amplitude at the interface
$$\frac BA=-e^{2iqX(L)},\qquad \left|\frac BA\right|=e^{-2qS(L)}.$$
This is the exact continuous one-mode error for a Dirichlet termination.

references.title: Steven G. Johnson, Notes on Perfectly Matched Layers (PMLs), §3.3
Michler, Demkowicz, Kurtz, and Pardo, Improving the performance of Perfectly Matched Layers by means of hp-adaptivity, §§2.1–2.2

items.title: Exact modal Dirichlet-to-Neumann map on a sphere
items.statement:
For $k>0$, $R>0$, and $g\in C^\infty(\mathbb S^2;\mathbb C)$, let $g_\ell$ be its $L^2(\mathbb S^2)$-orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H_\ell$ and set
$$\tau_\ell(k,R)=k\frac{(h_\ell^{(1)})'(kR)}{h_\ell^{(1)}(kR)},\qquad T_{k,R}g=\sum_{\ell=0}^\infty\tau_\ell(k,R)g_\ell.$$
The associated outgoing extension for $r\ge R$ is
$$v(r,\omega)=\sum_{\ell=0}^\infty\frac{h_\ell^{(1)}(kr)}{h_\ell^{(1)}(kR)}g_\ell(\omega).$$
The denominator is nonzero by [[lem-pe18-spherical-hankel-radial-identities]]. The convergence, smoothness, PDE, and radiation properties are asserted in [[thm-pe18-exact-spherical-dtn-map-on-smooth-data]].

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, Chapter 10: Bessel Functions
Plamen Stefanov, Scattering and Inverse Scattering in R^n, Appendix 1, §§1.1–1.2

items.title: Exact spherical-mode reflection under the local impedance truncation
items.statement:
Fix $k,R>0$ and $\ell\ge0$. On $r=R$, write one radial mode as $u(r)=A h_\ell^{(1)}(kr)+B h_\ell^{(2)}(kr)$, where $h_\ell^{(2)}=\overline{h_\ell^{(1)}}$. If $u$ satisfies $\partial_ru-iku=0$ at $R$, then
$$B=-\frac{(h_\ell^{(1)})'(kR)-ih_\ell^{(1)}(kR)}{(h_\ell^{(2)})'(kR)-ih_\ell^{(2)}(kR)}A.$$
The denominator is nonzero. For $A\ne0$, the exact reflected modal-amplitude ratio is therefore
$$\frac BA=-\frac{(h_\ell^{(1)})'(kR)-ih_\ell^{(1)}(kR)}{(h_\ell^{(2)})'(kR)-ih_\ell^{(2)}(kR)}.$$
If $A=0$, the coefficient equality forces $B=0$ and no ratio is defined. No uniform-in-$\ell$ smallness is asserted.

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, Chapter 10: Bessel Functions
NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §§10.49–10.50

items.title: Rellich uniqueness for the sound-soft spherical obstacle
items.statement: For $a>0$, $k>0$, and the convention in [[def-pe18-exterior-helmholtz-problem]], every classical outgoing solution of $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ on $r>a$ with zero Dirichlet trace at $r=a$ is identically zero.

references.title: Plamen Stefanov, Scattering and Inverse Scattering in R^n, Appendix 1, §§1.1–1.2
NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, Chapter 10: Bessel Functions

items.title: The spherical modal DtN map is well-defined and exact for smooth data
items.statement: For every $k,R>0$ and smooth $g$ on $\mathbb S^2$, the series in [[def-pe18-exact-spherical-dtn-map]] converges in $C^\infty(\mathbb S^2)$ to $T_{k,R}g$, and $|\tau_\ell(k,R)|\le k+(\ell+1)/R$. Its outgoing extension converges in $C^2$ on each compact annulus $R\le r\le R_1$, solves $(\Delta+k^2)v=0$, has trace $v(R,\cdot)=g$ and radial derivative $\partial_rv(R,\cdot)=T_{k,R}g$, and satisfies the uniform outgoing Sommerfeld condition as $r\to\infty$. It is the unique classical outgoing extension of $g$.

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, Chapter 10: Bessel Functions
NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §§10.49–10.52

items.title: Exact-DtN truncated modal variational formulation
items.statement:
Fix $0<a<R$ and $k>0$. The coefficient energy space $\mathcal V_{a,R}$ consists of sequences $u=(u_\ell)_{\ell\ge0}$ with $u_\ell\in H^1((a,R);\mathcal H_\ell)$ and
$$\|u\|_{\mathcal V}^2=\sum_{\ell=0}^\infty\int_a^R\left(r^2\|u_\ell'(r)\|_2^2+(1+\ell(\ell+1))\|u_\ell(r)\|_2^2\right)dr<\infty.$$
For smooth inner data $f$ on $\mathbb S^2$, let $f_\ell$ be its projection onto $\mathcal H_\ell$ and define the affine trial space $\mathcal V_f=\{u\in\mathcal V_{a,R}:u_\ell(a)=f_\ell\text{ for every }\ell\}$ and test space $\mathcal V_0=\{v\in\mathcal V_{a,R}:v_\ell(a)=0\text{ for every }\ell\}$. Traces and continuity of the following form are established in [[lem-pe18-modal-trace-and-form-continuity]]. With the inner product linear in its first argument, set
$$\mathfrak a_{k,a,R}(u,v)=\sum_{\ell=0}^\infty\int_a^R\left(r^2\langle u_\ell',v_\ell'\rangle+(\ell(\ell+1)-k^2r^2)\langle u_\ell,v_\ell\rangle\right)dr-R^2\sum_{\ell=0}^\infty\tau_\ell(k,R)\langle u_\ell(R),v_\ell(R)\rangle.$$
The exact-DtN variational problem is to find $u\in\mathcal V_f$ such that $\mathfrak a_{k,a,R}(u,v)=0$ for every $v\in\mathcal V_0$. The assigned theorem on this page proves existence and uniqueness.

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, Chapter 10: Bessel Functions
Plamen Stefanov, Scattering and Inverse Scattering in R^n, Appendix 1, §§1.1–1.2

items.title: Modal trace bound and continuity of the exact-DtN variational form
items.statement:
Fix $0<a<R$, $k>0$, and let $\mathcal V_{a,R}$ and $\mathfrak a_{k,a,R}$ be as in [[def-pe18-spherical-dtn-truncated-variational-problem]]. There is $C=C(a,R,k)$ such that for every $u,v\in\mathcal V_{a,R}$,
$$\sum_{\ell\ge0}(1+\ell)\bigl(\|u_\ell(a)\|_2^2+\|u_\ell(R)\|_2^2\bigr)\le C\|u\|_{\mathcal V}^2,\qquad |\mathfrak a_{k,a,R}(u,v)|\le C\|u\|_{\mathcal V}\|v\|_{\mathcal V}.$$
In particular, the defining traces and boundary pairing are finite, the form is continuous, $\mathcal V_{a,R}$ is a Hilbert direct sum, and finite-degree truncations converge in its norm.

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, Chapter 10: Bessel Functions
Plamen Stefanov, Scattering and Inverse Scattering in R^n, Appendix 1, §§1.1–1.2

items.title: Existence and uniqueness for the spherical exact-DtN variational problem
items.statement:
Fix $0<a<R$, $k>0$, and smooth $f$ on $\mathbb S^2$. The exact-DtN variational problem of [[def-pe18-spherical-dtn-truncated-variational-problem]] has exactly one solution $u\in\mathcal V_f$. It is the restriction to $a\le r\le R$ of the outgoing modal field
$$u(r,\omega)=\sum_{\ell=0}^\infty\frac{h_\ell^{(1)}(kr)}{h_\ell^{(1)}(ka)}f_\ell(\omega),$$
where $f_\ell$ is the degree-$\ell$ projection of $f$.

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, Chapter 10: Bessel Functions
Plamen Stefanov, Scattering and Inverse Scattering in R^n, Appendix 1, §§1.1–1.2

title: Exterior waves, absorbing boundaries and PML — Examples

items.title: PML attenuation vanishes at grazing and excludes evanescent modes
items.statement: For a propagating angle $0\le\theta<\pi/2$, $q=k\cos\theta$ and the one-way PML amplitude after accumulated stretch $S$ is $e^{-kS\cos\theta}$. It equals $e^{-kS}$ at normal incidence and tends to $1$ as $\theta\uparrow\pi/2$. For a purely evanescent normal branch $q=i\alpha$ with $\alpha>0$, the factor $e^{iqX}=e^{-\alpha x-i\alpha S(x)}$ has modulus $e^{-\alpha x}$, so this imaginary stretch adds no modulus decay.

references.title: Steven G. Johnson, Notes on Perfectly Matched Layers (PMLs), §§6, 7.2

items.title: Normal, oblique, and grazing impedance reflection
items.statement:
Write $q=k\cos\theta$ for $0\le\theta<\pi/2$. The reflected amplitude is
$$\mathcal R(\theta)=\frac{\cos\theta-1}{\cos\theta+1}.$$
It is $0$ at normal incidence, equals $-1/3$ at $\theta=\pi/3$, and tends to $-1$ at grazing incidence.

references.title: Galkowski, Lafontaine, and Spence, Local absorbing boundary conditions on fixed domains give order-one errors for high-frequency waves

items.title: A weakly damped truncated layer can produce a resonant cavity response
items.statement:
Consider the one-dimensional interval $0\le x\le L$ with Dirichlet endpoints, source point $x_0=L/2$, and a PML beginning at $x_0$, so $X(x_0)=x_0$ and $X(L)=L+iS$ with $S>0$. For $kL=(2m+1)\pi$, $m\in\mathbb N_0$, the Green function of $-d^2/dX^2-k^2$ at the source has magnitude
$$|G(x_0,x_0)|=\frac{\coth(kS)}{k}\sim\frac1{k^2S}\quad(S\downarrow0).$$
When $S=0$, $\sin(kx)$ is a nonzero homogeneous Dirichlet mode, so the real-frequency problem is resonant. This is a single interval example, not a universal stability claim about PMLs.

references.title: Steven G. Johnson, Notes on Perfectly Matched Layers (PMLs), §2

items.title: The outgoing monopole field of a sound-soft sphere
items.statement:
For constant boundary data $f=1$ on the sphere of radius $a$, the outgoing solution is
$$u(r)=\frac{h_0^{(1)}(kr)}{h_0^{(1)}(ka)}=\frac ar e^{ik(r-a)},\qquad r\ge a.$$

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §§10.49–10.52

items.title: The monopole symbol of the exact spherical DtN map
items.statement: Since $h_0^{(1)}(z)=-ie^{iz}/z$, its logarithmic derivative is $h_0'(z)/h_0(z)=i-z^{-1}$. Therefore the degree-zero exact spherical DtN multiplier at radius $R$ is $\tau_0(k,R)=ik-1/R$.

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, Chapter 10: Bessel Functions
